dedupe_keys.name: sociodemographic patterns of exposure to civil aircraft noise at 90 us airports simon et al ehp 2022

description: A national study by Boston University, the Volpe Center and Harvard researchers, published in Environmental Health Perspectives in 2022, of who is exposed to civil aircraft noise around US airports. Coverage: 90 US airports with day-night average sound level (DNL) contours developed for 2010 from 45 dB(A) upward in 1 dB steps; census block groups were counted as exposed when at least half their land lay within a threshold of 45, 55 or 65 dB(A). Methods: comparison of race and ethnicity, education and income of exposed and nearby unexposed block groups (4,031 to 74,253 per comparison) with multinomial and multilevel regressions. Outcome: block groups with more Hispanic residents, or more residents with only a high school education, had higher odds of exposure, with large differences between airports. Format and access: open journal article (DOI 10.1289/EHP9307). Licence and cost: free to read; the licence was not stated on the pages read. Caveats: 2010 contours only and block group aggregation. It shows how noise exposure layers can be joined to census data for equity analysis in hazard exposure models of airport operations. It relates to the US airport noise trends case study and the BTS National Transportation Noise Map in the catalogue.
